# ArcadeBench

ArcadeBench is a free, non-commercial, open-source arcade for humans and machines.

Arcade launcher: https://arcadebench.org/
Partition: https://arcadebench.org/games/partition/
Maltline: https://arcadebench.org/games/maltline/
About ArcadeBench: https://arcadebench.org/about/
Privacy promise: https://arcadebench.org/privacy/
Terms of play: https://arcadebench.org/terms/
Source: https://github.com/eanderson4/arcadebench

- Partition is a deterministic real-time territory game with a ten-stage human arcade run, an authored field catalog, controller interfaces, and tick-by-tick replay inspection.
- Maltline is a deterministic eight-stage shake-counter prototype: match orders, blend and slide shakes, and catch returning jars. It requires a keyboard and a window at least 700 CSS pixels wide.
- The root launcher starts neither game. Each permanent game route opens at its own home or title flow with replay and gameplay logic isolated from the launcher.
- ArcadeBench does not sell player data or use gameplay, replays, prompts, or controllers to train AI.
- A full replay is uploaded only for ranked-score verification or when Share is explicitly selected.
- New score submissions made under the Top 50 policy retain qualifying replays privately without scheduled expiration. Earlier submissions, nonqualifying score proofs, and shared replay links expire after five days. Social-media use requires a separate unchecked-by-default opt-in; no AI training.
- Permanent leaderboard records contain the public score summary and replay hash, not playable replay inputs.
- Callsign moderation sends only the proposed callsign to Cloudflare Workers AI; it never sends replay or controller data.
